candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — selection of a non-calcium phosphate binder in CKD-MBD
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize why a non-calcium phosphate binder such as sevelamer may be selected when phosphate lowering is needed but additional calcium-based binder exposure is being limited.

options.A: Sevelamer lowers phosphate without adding calcium, which can be useful when the treatment plan is intentionally limiting exposure to calcium-based phosphate binders.
options.B: Sevelamer is chosen because it provides a larger calcium load than calcium-based binders while lowering phosphate.
options.C: Sevelamer is administered intravenously and removes phosphate directly from the bloodstream during dialysis.
options.D: Sevelamer has no clinically relevant phosphate-binding effect and is used primarily as calcium supplementation.

candidate.rationale: KDIGO CKD-MBD guidance suggests restricting the dose of calcium-based phosphate binders in adults with CKD G3a-G5D receiving phosphate-lowering treatment. Sevelamer is a nonabsorbed, non-calcium phosphate-binding polymer that binds phosphate in the gastrointestinal tract and decreases its absorption. Therefore, using sevelamer can lower phosphate without adding calcium when limiting calcium-based binder exposure is clinically appropriate. B reverses its non-calcium property, C assigns an intravenous/dialytic mechanism it does not have, and D denies its phosphate-binding action.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports limiting calcium-based phosphate-binder exposure in adult CKD and using sevelamer as a phosphate-lowering binder that does not add a calcium-based binder load.
